title: wb register on one node renders its board over the hand-authored wip.md that wb migrate reads, so register then migrate carries an empty board
body:
`intent wb register <node> --name <n> --role <r>` renders the node's board views as soon as it writes the row, so the hand-authored `intent/whiteboard/<node>/wip.md` is overwritten with the empty row (session_id none, status paused, every section `_(none)_`) before `intent wb migrate <node>` can read it. migrate reads the working-tree file and refuses an unregistered node, so the documented order, register then migrate, carries an empty board unless the file is restored from git in between. Found in Gtools (gtools-vc, 2026-09-14): the board was committed at d2ac8c4, restored after register, then migrated.

Cause, read against the source at v3.0.2 (e75708756): `Facade::wb_register` ends with `self.land_board_write()`. The doc on `land_board_write` states the opposite rule for exactly this reason: the verbs that read hand-authored markdown do not call it, "the registration step would erase the board the migration after it exists to carry". It names `register_roster`, the roster-wide door, which holds to it; the single-node door does not.

Fix (shaped with issues on migrate's rendering and its unregistered-sender remedy, as one cutover-ordering change): single-node register writes the row and the index and no files, as `register_roster` does.

Same cutover family as 0374 (migrate carries entries as live past the bound) and 0375 (the hv board's standing directives have no kind to carry), which Gtools met too.

CLOSED 2026-09-14 15:44Z: `wb register` on a node with a hand-authored `wip.md` now registers it unmigrated and refreshes the index only, writing no file, so every board write refuses until `wb migrate` carries the board. A node with no `wip.md` is its row and still lands its view, because doctor reads a migrated node's absent view as missing. Fixed in the commit that closes this issue, with 0380 and 0381.
